Resolves #20591

🌿 *An application's palette can no longer lose to the engine's defaults on load order alone.*

The two `theme-neo-*/apps/workstation/Viewport.scss` sheets declare at `:root .neo-theme-neo-*` again, the weight `StylingAndTheming.md` gives an application projection. At `:where()` weight (since #18747) they tied the engine's dock values layer, whose per-class sheets load after the app's. As a result, in neo-light the Workstation's DEFAULT drop-preview accent painted the engine's `#0d9488` instead of its own `#0f766e`. In neo-dark every shared token resolves to the same value, so nothing changes there.

The light `--agent-dock-proxy-shadow` projection changes value. The app's ground colour is the near-invisible shadow the engine's light values sheet replaced on purpose. It becomes `color-mix(in srgb, var(--workstation-ink-dim) 45%, transparent)`, which computes to exactly the `rgba(90, 107, 128, 0.45)` the drag proxy carries today, now from the app's own palette. `preview-language-pair-light.png` is re-minted after the fix. Its only change is the DEFAULT inactive chip, which the July golden recorded with the dark `--dock-preview-ground` fallback.

Evidence: L2 (local visual and component runs on built dev themes at the head) → L2 required (AC-1 to AC-4 are rendered and computed-style outcomes; the visual tier is local-only by design). Residual: none.

## Deltas from ticket

- I corrected AC-2 in the ticket body before opening this PR. The raw residue outside the chip comes from the environment, so the AC now states the above-threshold result plus the byte-identical accents.
- The light proxy-shadow projection changes value instead of being dropped. I tried dropping it first; the Workstation skin-parity guard (`check-theme-surfaces`) and `DockPreview.spec.mjs:122` (every dock alias projected in both modes) both refused, which is their job. The ticket's Fix was updated to match.
- Grace, the author of the `:where()` policy, added two asks, both done. First, the sheets open with the precedent's comment shape (`dialog/Base.scss:1`), naming #18102. Second, a red-first CI arm pins the projection, because no guard caught the demotion.

## Test Evidence

- **Probe** (light arm, after the theme swap, built dev themes at the head): `--agent-dock-preview-accept` `#0f766e`, `--agent-dock-preview-accept-fill` `rgba(15, 118, 110, 0.14)`. The proxy shadow computes as `color(srgb 0.352941 0.419608 0.501961 / 0.45)`, which is `rgba(90, 107, 128, 0.45)`. On `dev`, the same probe read `#0d9488` (2/2), with sheet order `apps/workstation/Viewport.css` → `dashboard/Container.css` → `dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.css`.
- **Raw compare**, July golden against the fixed render, before the re-mint: 990 pixels differ, down from 57,840 on `dev`. 624 of them sit in the DEFAULT inactive chip and its shadow. The DEFAULT zone border (`48,136,130`) and split bar (`44,134,128`) match the golden byte for byte. The other 366 are the board's rounded-corner backdrop and label antialiasing.
- `NEO_E2E_PORT=8117 npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.visual.mjs`: 4/4 at the head; the dark golden is unchanged.
- Component tier: `DockSplitterPaint.spec.mjs` and `tooltip/ThemeProjection.spec.mjs`, 11/11.
- **Red-first** for `WorkstationThemeProjection.spec.mjs`: green 3/3 at the head; red 2/2 with `dev`'s two sheets restored and the themes rebuilt (`Expected "#0f766e"`, `Received "#0d9488"`).
- The other specs that read these sheets by path pass at the head: `DockRailTabPaint` + `DockSplitterPaint` 16/16, `WorkstationPaletteBridgeNL` 4/4, and the workstation component dir 7/7.
- All of the above were re-run at `0041e93b43` after a full dev theme rebuild. `npm run check-theme-surfaces` passes, and `test/playwright/unit/dashboard/DockPreview.spec.mjs` passes 32/32.
